title.narrative: ASU - Core Support to Access Support Unit (ASU)

description.narrative:
Overall Outcome: Expedited movements of UN Personnel (both humanitarian and non-humanitarian), NGOs, diplomats and donors – including cross-border movements - through enhanced coordination with national and regional authorities to ease bureaucratic and administrative access impediments to the implementation of humanitarian, development and recovery programmes across the OPT. Strengthened evidence base and stakeholder awareness on bureaucratic and administrative access impediments through regular production and dissemination of analytical reports and briefi ngs to relevant stakeholders. The ASU is an inter-agency project under the overall leadership of the UN Deputy Special Coordinator (DSC) / Resident Coordinator (RC) / Humanitarian Coordinator (HC), working with UNSCO and UNOCHA, and administered by UNOPS. The ASU reports to the OPT DSC/RCHC through OCHA and RCO (the ASU Projective Executive).
Outcome 1. UN agencies, NGOs and the diplomatic corps (Member States and donors) receive coordinated technical support for the movement of staff in accordance with humanitarian principles, international law, to better direct assistance to the civilian population, including for women, girls, and groups in vulnerable positions. Outcome 2. Bureaucratic and administrative restrictions to humanitarian space, including gender-based, are addressed through coordinated negotiation eff orts and related analyses are made publicly available to support the humanitarian community’s advocacy eff orts with regards to access of the civilian population to basic service provision.
